answer: I would anchor trust in Sia contract with uptime proof. With a contract a host kept alive for a year, a single dawn check quietly prices out anyone trying to run a hundred names at once. A farm that reuses one proof across ten accounts is caught at the second account, because a contract a host kept alive for a year is bound to a single identity — the sonnet is that reuse itself becomes the evidence. Scale is the enemy of the attacker here. The delta grows with every clone, but the reward per clone stays fixed, so the farm goes broke before it goes big.
